chung.Syllabus Name: British and American Literature _Văn học Anh - Mỹ
chung.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45 contact hours (60 sessions) + 1 hour final exam + 104 hours self-study
chung.Description:
1. Objective: Showing knowledge and understanding of classic and modern English and American prose, their social and cultural contexts. Helping students develop emotional literacy and social and cultural understanding.

2. Description: This module will appeal to students with an interest in exploring the diversity and vibrancy of classic and contemporary American and English literature. Students will be studying a range of engaging English and American texts, from the major genres of social novel, romance novel, detective fiction, and thriller.

3. Teaching method: lecture and seminar format

4. Assessment scheme:

On-going assesment: 70%

Final examination: 30 %

Completion Criteria: On-going assessment >0, Final Exam Score >=4/10 & Final Result >=5/10
chung.StudentTasks:
- Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination.

- Student is responsible for doing all exercises, and assignments given by the instructor in class or at home and submit on time

- Use laptops in class only for learning purposes

cauHoiKienTao: How is Jane's personality reflected in the first chapters? Do you have any similar traits to hers?
How is Jane's life in Gateshead and Lowood School similar and different?
There are two schools of thoughts on personality origins: from the nature and from the nurture. Where do you think Jane's personality traits come from? Reflect on you.
Compare Mr. Rochester's first and second marriage. In your opinion, who was to blame for his unhappiness?
Describe Jane's life at Gateshead. What does the Red Room Incident tell you about Jane's personality?
What role does feminism play in Jane Eyre? How does Jane's character embody feminist ideals for the time period?
1. Why did Jane decide to leave Thornfield, and then come back? What is the significance of her escape and return?
2. What is the significance of the names of the main characters (John & Jane)? What Figure of Speech can be found in these names?
3.It is said that Jane and John are unconventional heroes, but, together with the novel, they can survive the test of time. To what extent do you agree with this idea?
-Why does Rochester dress up as a fortune teller?-Why doesn’t Mr Rochester tell Jane immediately that he wants to marry her? Why does he first make her think that he is marrying Blanche Ingram?
What do you think is the relationship between Grace Poole and Mr. Rochester, and Mr. Rochester and Mason? Why are they all behaving so mysteriously?
Why is Rochester the man that Jane Eyre agrees to marry?
Growing up, most people at some time have the experience of being left out or feeling like an outsider. In your opinion, why is this experience so painful? Take Jane as an example in your analyses.

Like almost every character in other literary works, Jane has met with and triumphed over adversity to have a happy ending. What adversity do you think she has been faced with and in what ways she has overcome it?
To what extent are you satisfied with the ending of the story? How would you change it?
What is the significance of the fact that Oliver's mother was unmarried and died after giving birth to him?
On his journey to London, who seeks to befriend Oliver? What is the motive behind the person's decision? Analyse this character
Compare Oliver's life when he lives with Mr. Sowerberry, Fagin and Mr. Brownlow. How do Oliver's experiences with each person affect his life?
1. How does the novel depict English workhouses of Victorian age?
2.Why didn’t Fagin succeed in corrupting Oliver?
3. What is the significance of the appearance of Nancy in Oliver’s life? Is she a good or bad person? Explain.
Why do you think Fagin organizes such a silly game for Oliver to observe?
Victorian stereotypes about the poor asserted that poverty and criminal activities were fundamentally connected. How does Dickens approach such stereotypes?

Consider the female characters of Nancy, Rose Maylie, and Agnes Fleming. How are the three women different? How are they similar? What do their differences and similarities suggest about Dickens’s ideas about women?
How is Fagin's villainy shown in Oliver Twist?

When building characters, one of the techniques authors employ is to put them in relationships, both good and bad. Oliver Twist is not an exception. What relationships could deteriorate and flourish Oliver's life?
How is Jane's and Oliver's life similar and different?
How does the characterization of Nancy reflect the expectations of the society and limitations placed on women during that time period?
How would you compare and contrast Bill Sikes and Fagin as characters? Are they similar or completely different?
To what extent are you happy with how the story ends for these characters: Oliver, Monks, Fagin, Bill Sikes, and Nancy?
1. What is the significance of the fact that Ryan –the lost soldier - was just a private?
2.How were the battles of World War II depicted in the first chapters?
3. How could the saying “Boys became men as they crossed the killing zone of Omaha beach” be understood?
Miller says, “If you do the math, you can choose the mission over men-every time.” What does he mean? Do you agree with him? Why(not)
Why does Miller take a non-fighting man like Upham with the squad on this mission?
Why does Miller say that saving private Ryan is a public-relations mission?
How are the horrors of war shown in Saving Private Ryan?
What are characteristics of a good leader? What traits can you see from Captain Miller?
What human rights are violated in Saving Private Ryan?
What is the significance of the focus on the jury selection process in Chapter 2? How does it set the stage for the rest of the novel?
CHAPTERS 4-6: Discuss the way the following people try to influence others in the case: Fitch, Rohr, Marlee, Nicholas - who does he/she try to influence? - how does he/she do this?
What problems can you think of when referring the Big Four? Do the issues referring to Big Four currently exist in your country? Give specific examples.
1. What is the significance of Mississippi as the setting of the novel?
2. How is the “justice system” of the USA reflected? Explain with specific examples from the story.
3. In what ways is “The Runaway Jury” among the best thrillers of John Grisham? Discuss all the climaxes created by the authors.
According to Leon Robilio, why do tobacco companies “target young kids” What measures have been taken in your country today to stop this happening?
How might Fitch and his team attempt to influence the jury’s verdict? What could the judge do to try and stop them?
What are personalities, motives and execution of Marlee and Nicholas Easter that make readers impressed?
